_source: Row counts measured by Plan 103-01 on 2026-07-31 from a candidate built offline by scripts/rebuild-golden.sh at v2.7-20-g7f121cc, and reconciled model-by-model against production. The classified difference table is in .planning/phases/103-rebuild-golden-and-gates/103-01-rebuild-evidence-2026-07-31.txt SS4.
notes: Per-model row counts a rebuilt candidate MUST produce before it may become the golden snapshot.

WHY EVERY TOLERANCE IS ZERO. The rebuild makes no network calls and contains no randomness: parcels come from the committed data/merced/selected_parcels.geojson, flowlines from the committed data/merced/flowlines.json, and evapotranspiration from the committed data/merced/openet_cache.json. The same tree therefore has to produce the same numbers every time. A count that moves is not variance -- it is a change somebody made, and this gate's job is to make them say so in writing before it ships. A non-zero tolerance would have to name what varies and why; nothing here qualifies, so nothing here has one.

WHY NOT '> 0'. A check that only asserts not-zero passes a demonstration that quietly lost ninety percent of its rows and still renders every page. That is the precise failure this file exists to catch, so the comparison is equality against a written-down number.

SHAPE IS NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN. Production and staging once differed in only seven tables by COUNT while three tables held identical counts and completely different names. This is gate 2 of four; gates 1 and 4 read content.
WHEN A SEED CHANGE FAILS THIS GATE: that is the design, not a bug. Update the entry, change the reason to say what moved and why, and commit both together with the seed change.

accounting.AllocationCarryover.reason: Written by seed_merced's allocation step, one row per account carrying unused allocation out of the closed reporting period. Fixed by the account set and the period definition, both committed.

accounting.AllocationPlan.reason: One plan per water account per reporting period, created by seed_merced. Moves only if the account set or the number of periods changes.

accounting.CalculationPlan.reason: The single methodology version the demonstration is locked to, created by seed_calculation_plan. A second row means a methodology was added without the version lock being considered (Phase 42).

accounting.CalculationRun.reason: Output of refresh_merced_accounting over the committed parcel set. 103-01 reproduced production's 912 exactly, of which 362 are zero-precipitation runs. This is the number that proves the engine ran and produced the same answer as the live site; a candidate with 0 here has data but no accounting.

accounting.CalculationStep.reason: The five ordered steps of the locked calculation plan. Structural, not data -- a change here is a methodology change.

accounting.ReportingPeriod.reason: The two water years the demonstration covers. The ET cache holds exactly one window (WY 2024-25), so adding a period without extending the cache would produce empty accounting for it.

accounting.WaterAccount.reason: The invented accounts seed_merced creates. Every holder name here is fabricated by design; gate 1 is what proves that separately.

accounting.WaterAccountParcel.reason: One row per parcel, tying each to its account. Must equal parcels.Parcel exactly -- a lower number means parcels exist that no account is responsible for, which renders as blank accounting rather than an error.

accounting.WaterCredit.reason: Banked-water credits created by seed_merced to exercise the credit ledger. Fixed set.

accounting.WaterCreditDraw.reason: Draws against credits are a visitor action, not seeded content. Non-zero in a candidate means the build captured somebody's session.

accounting.WaterType.reason: Reference data from seed_data: the water types the accounting engine apportions across. Production carries the same 6.

core.Role.reason: Reference data from seed_roles. Roles are structure; the users that would hold them are deliberately absent.

core.SiteConfig.reason: The single site configuration row. Zero means the deployment has no identity and the header renders unbranded.

core.User.reason: THE POINT OF THE WHOLE MILESTONE. The rebuild never boots a serving web container, so entrypoint.sh's no-argument branch -- and with it ensure_superuser -- never runs. A non-zero count means a deployment's admin account got baked into an artifact that ships to production. That is the exact mechanism by which staging admin rows once reached production, and it is why every step of rebuild-golden.sh is 'run --rm' rather than 'up web'. Production's own admin returns from its .env on the next container boot after a restore, so nothing is lost by shipping zero.

core.UserRole.reason: Follows core.User. A role assignment cannot exist without a user to assign it to, so any non-zero count here means the same leak.

datasync.DataRecordStaging.reason: The demonstration's frozen telemetry: two water years (2024-10-01 onward) for the 42 active stations, loaded from data/merced/readings.json by load_reading_fixture. The previous pin of 0 was right about build hygiene and wrong about the demonstration -- the build makes no network call, so an unfrozen table meant every station chart on the site was blank while the landing hero, reading a frozen last_data_at, announced '37 of 42 stations reporting'. Found on production 2026-08-01, minutes after the v2.8 cutover. The count is the generator's own output, not an estimate: dump_reading_fixture keeps the last real reading of each (station, parameter, calendar day) and two consecutive dumps of the same database were byte-identical (sha256 89b8ec28...). Tolerance stays 0 because nothing here is sampled or random -- if this number moves, the fixture was regenerated and that is a change somebody made.

datasync.DataSource.reason: Reference data: the external data sources the platform knows how to pull from. Definitions, not fetched records.

datasync.DataSyncLog.reason: One row per sync pull performed. Zero because the build performs none.

datasync.MonitoredStation.reason: Frozen into data/merced/stations.json and loaded by load_station_fixture, for the same reason data/merced/flowlines.json is frozen: a gate that reddens because an upstream catalogue had a bad afternoon is a gate people learn to ignore. The demonstration's own about page lists these stations under 'Real published records -- USGS and CDEC', beside the river network, so they are demonstration content and not somebody else's registry passing through. 335 total, 42 of them is_active -- and 42 is the number the landing-page hero displays. Tolerance 0 is correct precisely because the count cannot move unless data/merced/stations.json moves. Supersedes the 103-01 reasoning that stations need not be frozen because no later seed step reads MonitoredStation: that judged them by what the build consumes rather than by what the demonstration shows.

datasync.OpenETCache.reason: 76 parcels x 5 variables x 1 window (WY 2024-25), loaded from the committed data/merced/openet_cache.json by load_openet_fixture. 103-01 predicted 380 and measured 380, and proved the staging and production caches byte-identical by sha256. Without these rows the accounting engine has no demand side and every calculation run comes out empty.

drinking.Analyte.reason: Reference data: the contaminant list the drinking-water module reports against. Published regulatory content, seeded.

drinking.EnvirofactsCache.reason: Cached responses committed as fixture data so the build stays offline. Not fetched at build time -- if this required a network call the rebuild would not be reproducible.

drinking.RegulatoryLimit.reason: Reference data: published maximum contaminant levels. Real published record, carried as published.

drinking.SampleEvent.reason: Real published sampling events for the demonstration water system. Carried as published and labelled on screen, per the honesty doctrine.

drinking.SampleResult.reason: The lab results behind those events -- the largest single table in the demonstration. 103-01 reproduced production's 22,367 exactly. A collapse here would empty the drinking-water pages that Phase 92-99 built, while every page still rendered.

drinking.SamplingPoint.reason: The sampling points those events belong to. Published record.

drinking.SystemFacility.reason: Facilities of the demonstration water system. Published record.

drinking.WaterSystem.reason: The single water system the drinking-water module demonstrates. Zero would leave the drinking front door pointing at nothing -- which is exactly what production served from the 7/27 launch until this milestone, because the domain was empty on prod and nobody could tell from the repository.

feedback.Feedback.reason: Visitor submissions. Never build output. Production carries these and reset-demo.sh deliberately preserves them across the nightly restore; a candidate must not carry anybody's message.

feedback.FeedbackAttachment.reason: Screenshots attached to visitor submissions. Same reasoning as feedback.Feedback.

geography.Boundary.reason: The subbasin boundary, created by seed_merced_base before the flowlines load. It must exist first: flowlines.json names it by natural key, and its primary key differs between deployments (1 on staging, 6 on production), which is why the fixture keys on the name rather than the pk.

geography.Flowline.reason: Loaded from the committed data/merced/flowlines.json fixture (Phase 102-02, 7.5 MB). This fixture is what lets the build skip auto_populate -- the only networked step in the eleven-step seed. seed_merced --skip-auto-populate refuses up front if the fixture is not loaded, so a zero here should be impossible rather than merely wrong.

geography.ParcelZone.reason: Parcel-to-zone memberships, derived from the committed parcel and zone geometry by spatial intersection. Deterministic given both inputs.

geography.Zone.reason: The management zones the subbasin is divided into. Committed geometry.

geography.ZoneGroup.reason: Zone grouping is an operator feature the demonstration does not exercise. Empty by design, not by omission.

health.HealthCheckResult.reason: Cron output on a running deployment. Production carries 321. A build produces none, and shipping a golden full of another machine's health history would make the health page lie about this one.

measurements.Meter.reason: The meters seed_merced installs on wells. Must stay equal to wells.WellMeter.

measurements.MeterReading.reason: Monthly totalizer reads on the 12 certified meters across WY 2024-2025 (12 x 12), written by seed_merced_measurements (Phase 132). Each month's delta is READ OFF the ParcelLedger meter_reading rows for the parcels that well irrigates, not invented -- so this number moves only if the meter set or the ledger's month coverage moves, and a change in one without the other is the regression to look for. read_by is NULL on every row: gate 2 requires core.User = 0.

measurements.Sensor.reason: One pressure transducer, on MER-W-004 -- the single monitoring well whose own declaration reads 'Continuous' (transducer logs daily). The other two monitoring wells declare a manual sounder and a quarterly sweep, so installing an instrument on either would contradict the demonstration's own note about it. A second row means a sensor was added to a well that did not declare one.

measurements.SensorMeasurement.reason: One logged reading a day for WY 2024-2025 (2024-10-01..2025-09-30) from the single transducer. DAILY IS THE CEILING, not a starting point: PROJECT.md puts real-time telemetry out of scope, so this is a logger downloaded on a field round. A count above 365 means something began polling.

measurements.WaterMeasurement.reason: Hand-entered depth-to-water readings at the cadence each monitoring well declares: MER-W-001 monthly (12), MER-W-002 quarterly (4), and 4 quarterly steel-tape checks against the transducer on MER-W-004. The checks sit a few hundredths off the logger on purpose -- that disagreement is what the quality flag exists to carry. recorded_by is NULL on every row.

parcels.CropType.reason: Reference data from seed_data. Production carries 7 because two rows (Citrus, Pistachios) are residue from the retired Demo Valley and Kaweah datasets that no current seed command creates. The CANDIDATE is the correct side of that difference -- this is exactly the accumulated accident a build-from-source replaces.

parcels.Parcel.reason: The selection is committed in data/merced/selected_parcels.geojson and seed_merced_parcels_from_selection.py has zero randomness in it, so this number cannot legitimately move without that file moving. Every other per-parcel count in this file is anchored to it: OpenETCache is 76 x 5, WaterAccountParcel is 76, UsageLocation is 76.

parcels.ParcelLedger.reason: The keyed water ledger entries the accounting engine writes per parcel per period. Derived output -- a shortfall here means the engine ran partially, which no page would show as an error.

parcels.ParcelStaging.reason: Landing table for bulk parcel import, an operator workflow. Empty in a build.

parcels.UsageLocation.reason: One usage location per parcel. Must equal parcels.Parcel.

recharge.RechargeEvent.reason: Managed aquifer recharge events across the seven sites, created by seed_merced to exercise the recharge ledger.

recharge.RechargeMeasurement.reason: Twelve on-site readings at each of the 7 basins (ponded depth, canal inflow, percolation, source-water TDS) across the four wet-season fills seed_merced_recharge_events writes. THE ONLY SLICE OF PHASE 132 WITH A SCREEN: the recharge detail page renders the ten most recent, and before this the card read 'No measurements recorded.' on all seven pages. Moves if the basin count or the fill schedule moves.

recharge.RechargeSite.reason: The seven recharge basins. Committed geometry and invented names.

recharge.RechargeSitePOD.reason: Links each recharge site to the point of diversion that supplies it (Phase 62). One per site.

reporting.ReportSubmission.reason: THE CANDIDATE IS THE CORRECT SIDE HERE. Production carries 11 rows that have been restored nightly since early June: orphan drafts with no user attached, all still in draft, ten of the eleven pointing at a file that does not exist. They are test artifacts that got photocopied into a golden and have been coming back every night for eight weeks. A build produces none, which is the whole thesis of this milestone in one line.

reporting.ReportTemplate.reason: Reference data: the state report formats (GEARS, CalWATRS) the platform can generate. Definitions, not filings.

reporting.ReportingCrosswalk.reason: Per-agency field mapping, configured by an operator against their own filing requirements. Not demonstration content.

reporting.ReportingProfile.reason: Follows ReportingCrosswalk -- operator configuration, not seeded.

standards.Datastream.reason: Production carries exactly one row created by no non-test code anywhere in the repository -- found by 103-01 and recorded in ISS-105. The candidate having none is correct.

standards.ObservedProperty.reason: The SensorThings crosswalk, seeded by seed_observed_properties. 17 until Phase 132 added `extracted_volume` -- the concept a totalizer meter actually reads, which nothing in the vocabulary meant: reservoir_storage carries the right UCUM atom (acre-foot) and entirely the wrong concept. Its USGS pcode is blank, the documented non-blocking exception (decision 31-01). THIS WAS ZERO IN THE FIRST CANDIDATE and no test and no page would ever have shown it: the standards app ships no views and no urls. seed_observed_properties sits outside the seed_data umbrella deliberately (core/modules.py:320-324), so the build sequence has to call it by name. It is the table check_conformance and every adapter's PARAMETER_MAP resolve against. Fixed in 7f121cc; this entry is the tripwire that keeps it fixed.

standards.SourceParameter.reason: The other half of the same crosswalk, and the other half of the same defect -- 0 vs production's 26 until 7f121cc. Together with ObservedProperty this is the +43 rows that took the candidate from 32,275 to 32,318.

surface.CurtailmentOrder.reason: One curtailment order, so the demonstration exercises the curtailment path at all. Invented.

surface.DiversionRecord.reason: Reported diversions across the nine points of diversion. Invented records on real river geometry -- the river is protected published fact, the diverters are not.

surface.PointOfDiversion.reason: The nine points of diversion. Their names are protected published record (Crocker-Huffman River Diversion, Snelling Re-Diversion and so on); the rights attached to them are invented.

surface.PointOfDiversionParcel.reason: Which parcels each point of diversion serves. Must stay equal to surface.WaterRightParcel.

surface.UnallocatedDelivery.reason: Deliveries not yet apportioned to a parcel, exercising the shared-supply apportionment path (Phase 56). MOVED 13 -> 14 by Plan 131-01, which sizes each served parcel's delivery as its measured demand divided by its own crop's irrigation-method efficiency (alfalfa 0.62 border-check flood through almonds 0.87 micro/drip) instead of a flat band keyed on the point-of-diversion's index. allocate_district_delivery caps every parcel at demand / the AGENCY-WIDE efficiency (SiteConfig, 0.750) because the kernel takes one efficiency per call and changing that would be an engine change; a POD whose crop mix is flood-heavy enough now records more than those caps explain, and the kernel writes the surplus as an UnallocatedDelivery rather than dropping it. Exactly one POD-month crossed that threshold: MER-POD-007-DEMO Plainsburg El Nido Canal Headgate, 2025-02, 5.3447 AF surplus of 45.4828 AF delivered. Observed both ways -- 13 rows with the pre-change seeder, 14 with it, on the same tree and the same data. Every other pinned count held, ParcelLedger at 1271 and DiversionRecord at 85 included.

surface.WaterRight.reason: Six invented water rights. Their holder_name column is the single most dangerous field in the database: it is where four real district names sat on production for three days in July 2026 beneath a page promising the demonstration names no real water district at all. Gate 1 reads it.

surface.WaterRightParcel.reason: Parcels served by each right. Equal to PointOfDiversionParcel by construction.

surface.WaterRightType.reason: Reference data from seed_data. Production carries 7 because of a bare 'Appropriative' row left over from the retired Demo Valley dataset. The candidate is the correct side.

wells.MonitoringWell.reason: The three ag wells that double as water-level monitoring points, written by seed_merced_measurements (Phase 132). Zero until then, and the reason mattered: the declarations lived only in scripts/export_merced_native.py, an export for the native app, so wells/partials/_detail_pane.html rendered a Monitoring section that had never had a row to show. Carried across verbatim rather than re-invented -- agency, frequency, reference elevation and datum, including the deliberate NGVD29 legacy-datum row on MER-W-004. Every instrument's cadence is read off measurement_frequency here.

wells.Well.reason: The 45 wells seed_merced creates. Their names are protected published record (Le Grand Ag Well and the rest); their owners are invented.

wells.WellIrrigatedParcel.reason: Which parcels each well irrigates -- the groundwater side of the mixed-use accounting the platform exists to do.

wells.WellMeter.reason: Meters installed on wells. Must equal measurements.Meter; a mismatch means one side was seeded and the other was not.

wells.WellType.reason: Reference data from seed_data. Production carries 7 because Domestic and Municipal are legacy rows no current seed creates. The candidate is the correct side.
